label: Temple
_model: Interior kernel, older and stranger than a church. A temple wants the rite performed exactly, to be fed, to keep its name unsaid, or to be the only one. Its accommodations are what a priesthood does when a god is literal.

appetites.want: to have the rite performed exactly
appetites.purpose: the words would never be got wrong

appeasement.move: copy whatever gesture is being made, exactly and without hurrying

appetites.purpose: the altar would never be dry

appeasement.move: give up something you will actually miss, at the altar
appeasement.why: it has been given something that cost

appetites.want: never to have its name said aloud

appeasement.move: say nothing at all for a full exchange, and let the silence stand

appetites.want: to be the only one worshipped here
appetites.purpose: no other name would ever be spoken here

appeasement.move: put away or cover any token of another faith you carry
appeasement.why: it is the only one here

accommodations.text: initiated {conscript} into a mystery they could not survive knowing
offered {conscript} on the stone, in order, over years
took the tongues of {conscript} so the name could not be said
veiled {conscript} and would not let them be looked at again
cast {conscript} out and had their gods broken in the street
bound {conscript} to the service and did not release them

tablet.label: the tablet with the rite cut correctly
tablet.function: the only complete copy of the words

knife.label: the knife the offerings were made with
knife.function: the only thing the altar has ever accepted

veil.label: the veil that was never lifted
veil.function: the only thing that has kept the name safe

idol.label: the idol that outlasted all the others
idol.function: the last one standing when the rest were broken

factions.name: the Celebrants
factions.essence: still performing a rite that has no ending written

factions.name: tomb-robbers
factions.essence: here for gold and out of their depth

factions.name: the Tongueless
factions.essence: keeping a name they can no longer say

factions.name: the broken gods
factions.essence: cast out and still in the building

triggerGlossary.announced: came up the processional way, upright, as a celebrant would
triggerGlossary.seenTwice: reflected in lamp-oil, or seen by two of the Tongueless
triggerGlossary.loud: a word said aloud in a place built to carry words
triggerGlossary.lingering: stayed still long enough for the rite to include you
triggerGlossary.disturbed: touched, moved or uncovered something set apart

foes.name: Skeleton
foes.note: fearless; will not break the procession

skirmish.avoid: walk in step with them and they take you for celebrants

fight.line: 1 Ghoul in the sacrifice pit and 2 Skeletons

foes.name: Ghoul
foes.note: free Called Shot to freeze on a hit

fight.avoid: it is fed on a schedule and will not leave the pit if the offering is made

foes.name: Necromancer
foes.note: raises one per round while the rite continues

battle.harmedBy: anything — but interrupting the rite stops the raising
battle.avoid: he cannot break off mid-rite; wait for the pause and he will parley

nightmare.line: 1 Wraith of the Veiled One, 1 Ghoul and 4 Skeletons

foes.name: Wraith
foes.note: INCORPOREAL — chill touch ignores armour, drains 1 max Grit

nightmare.harmedBy: blessed, silvered or magical weapons for the Wraith ONLY; anything for the rest
nightmare.avoid: it does not strike anyone who has said nothing

exactness.dangerLine: the rite is still being performed, and it notices a wrong hand

institution: floor-marks showing where each celebrant stands, worn deep
a rite cut into the walls in three languages, all agreeing
lamps in a pattern that is clearly not decorative
ritual: a procession stepping the same eleven paces, over and over
hands raised and lowered on a count nobody gives
a cup passed along a line with a gap in it
demand: a floor-mark exactly your size, empty
a doorway you must enter with a particular foot first
a hall that makes you aware you are doing it wrong
wound: a wall where the rite is cut wrongly and then corrected, twice
celebrants' hands broken and reset in the correct position
a tablet with an error scratched out so hard the stone split
anchor: a tablet with the rite cut correctly, once
a master copy under glass, unweathered
a lead sheet with the words punched into it

features: a floor-mark scrubbed brighter than the rest
a lamp moved out of the pattern
fresh chalk correcting a carved line
a cup set down mid-passage
a robe folded wrongly and refolded
footprints in ash, eleven paces, repeating

decisions.cue: a floor-mark exactly your size, empty in the line
decisions.cost: standing on it joins the rite

resolve.success: you take the place and step the measure correctly — the Celebrants accept you
resolve.failure: you step it wrongly and the rite must begin again: lose a Turn, +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: stay off the marks; the procession goes round you, coldly

decisions.cue: a rite cut on the wall in three languages that do not quite agree
decisions.cost: one of them is the correct one

resolve.success: you find the version the others were copied from and know the true form
resolve.failure: you pick a corrupted copy and are confidently wrong for the rest of the delve
resolve.orElse: copy all three and decide later: one Turn

decisions.cue: a doorway you must enter with a particular foot first
decisions.cost: which foot is not written anywhere obvious

resolve.success: you read it off the floor-wear and enter correctly
resolve.failure: you enter wrongly and the temple resets you to the previous room
resolve.orElse: go through the servants' arch: one Turn, and it is beneath you

decisions.cue: a cup being passed along a line with a gap where you stand
decisions.cost: taking it commits you; refusing breaks the line

resolve.success: you take, pass and are counted a celebrant for the rest of the delve
resolve.failure: you fumble the pass and the line stops: everything turns to look
resolve.orElse: step out of the line before it reaches you: the rite pauses, and resumes without you

decisions.cue: a tablet with an error scratched out hard enough to split the stone
decisions.cost: the correction matters more than the error

resolve.success: you read the correction and know one thing the temple insists on
resolve.failure: you read only the error and act on it once, wrongly
resolve.orElse: leave it; you go on not knowing

decisions.cue: lamps arranged in a pattern with one lamp out of place
decisions.cost: restoring it is either piety or interference

resolve.success: you set it right and the pattern completes — the temple opens a way it had closed
resolve.failure: you move the wrong lamp and the pattern is broken worse: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave the pattern; the way stays shut

situations.doing: stepping a measure with a gap in the line where one is missing
situations.onArrival: the gap arrives in front of you
situations.because: the measure requires eleven and there are ten
situations.offer: step the measure and they will carry you to the middle sanctum

situations.doing: correcting a carved line with a chisel, again
situations.onArrival: it offers you the chisel, handle first
situations.because: the text has never once been right
situations.offer: cut one correct character and it will read you the whole rite

situations.doing: copying wall-text they cannot read onto wax
situations.onArrival: they look up, guilty, and offer to share
situations.because: they are selling the rite to somebody
situations.offer: tell them what it says and they will tell you what is in the treasury

situations.doing: travelling along a line of hands toward you
situations.onArrival: the hand before yours holds it out
situations.because: the passing must not stop
situations.offer: take it and pass it, and the line lets you through

situations.doing: holding a gesture and waiting to be released from it
situations.onArrival: its arms are shaking, which should not be possible
situations.because: the next word of the rite was never spoken
situations.offer: say any word with authority and it lowers its arms and thanks you

situations.doing: going out one at a time in the pattern's order
situations.onArrival: the nearest gutters as you enter
situations.because: the pattern is completing itself, wrongly
situations.offer: relight one out of order and the temple loses count, which helps you

temptations.cue: a tablet with the rite cut correctly
temptations.benefit: once, perform any rite here exactly right
temptations.standingDrawback: the temple expects you to perform the rest of it

temptations.cue: a chip of a floor-mark
temptations.benefit: once, take somebody's place in a formal order
temptations.standingDrawback: whoever you displaced is looking for their place

temptations.cue: a lead sheet with the words punched in
temptations.benefit: once, say something so exactly it cannot be argued with
temptations.standingDrawback: you cannot say the same thing twice differently

temptations.cue: the Hierophant's chisel
temptations.benefit: once, correct something written and make it true
temptations.standingDrawback: the previous version begins to want to be restored

temptations.cue: one lamp from the pattern
temptations.benefit: once, make a place behave as the temple intends
temptations.standingDrawback: the pattern is short a lamp and the temple is searching

sacrifice.dangerLine: the altar is dry, and the temple has been waiting a long time

institution: channels cut into the floor, all sloping the same way
a stone with a hollow and a lip at one end
hooks in a beam at the height of a hanging thing
ritual: a beast led up the steps by nobody, nightly
a knife laid out, cleaned, and laid out again
a bowl carried in full and carried out empty
demand: a stone with a hollow exactly the size of a person's chest
a channel that runs toward you when you stand still
a room that makes you count how many of you there are
wound: channels scoured white by too much use
a pit under the floor, filled and filled again
a knife broken deliberately and the pieces kept apart
anchor: the knife itself, clean, on a folded cloth
a bowl that has never been washed
a ledger of what was given and on what day

features: a channel scrubbed clean, recently
a beast tethered and left
a knife laid out on fresh cloth
the pit lid moved aside
blood that has not dried in a dry room
a bowl set out, empty and waiting

decisions.cue: an altar with a hollow and a channel, and nothing on it
decisions.cost: the temple will take something either way

resolve.success: you give something that costs you and the altar is satisfied for the delve
resolve.failure: you give something worthless and it is refused: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: give nothing; the altar takes an opportunity later instead

decisions.cue: a beast tethered at the steps, left by somebody
decisions.cost: freeing it or offering it are both decisions

resolve.success: you make the offering properly and the temple grants you passage
resolve.failure: you free it and the temple takes the loss out of your reckoning: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it tethered; it is still there when you come back

decisions.cue: a knife broken in two and the halves kept apart
decisions.cost: joining them is the obvious thing and obviously unwise

resolve.success: you join them and hold the only thing the altar accepts
resolve.failure: you join them and the knife wants using: it is +1 Bane per area to carry
resolve.orElse: leave the halves apart; nothing is armed

decisions.cue: a pit under a moved lid, and something at the bottom
decisions.cost: what is down there was given, not thrown

resolve.success: you go down and come back with what was given, and the temple allows it
resolve.failure: you fall the last of it: 2 Grit, and something down there notices
resolve.orElse: leave the lid; the pit keeps what it was given

decisions.cue: a bowl carried in full and set down empty in front of you
decisions.cost: the bowl is asking

resolve.success: you fill it with something of yours and the Celebrants become helpful
resolve.failure: you fill it with water and the insult is understood: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: hand it back empty; the bowl waits for someone else

decisions.cue: a ledger of what was given and on what day, with today blank
decisions.cost: writing in it commits you to giving

resolve.success: you enter something already spent and the day is counted paid
resolve.failure: you enter a promise and the temple will collect: +1 Bane at the ending
resolve.orElse: leave the day blank; the temple notices the gap

situations.doing: standing tethered at the top of the steps, quite calm
situations.onArrival: it turns its head and looks at you without alarm
situations.because: it was led up and nobody came to take it
situations.offer: untie it and lead it out, and the temple counts the debt deferred

situations.doing: cleaning a knife that is already clean
situations.onArrival: it sets the knife down between you and it
situations.because: the offering hour came and nothing was brought
situations.offer: bring it anything living and it will open the inner doors

situations.doing: arguing beside an open pit about who goes down
situations.onArrival: they stop and one offers you a rope
situations.because: what is down there is worth having
situations.offer: hold the rope and they will share what comes up

situations.doing: running with something in a room where nothing has been cut
situations.onArrival: the flow moves toward your feet
situations.because: the altar is being fed from somewhere
situations.offer: follow the channels back and you find what is being given

situations.doing: holding a bowl out at arm's length, waiting
situations.onArrival: its arms do not lower
situations.because: the bowl has not been filled in three centuries
situations.offer: fill it and every Celebrant in the temple will stand aside

situations.doing: sitting warm in a cold room with the hollow wet
situations.onArrival: the wetness is fresh
situations.because: something was given here very recently
situations.offer: find out what, and the temple treats you as party to it

temptations.cue: the offering knife, clean
temptations.benefit: once, an attack cannot be defended against
temptations.standingDrawback: the temple counts what you take with it as given to it

temptations.cue: a bowl that has never been washed
temptations.benefit: once, make an offering count double
temptations.standingDrawback: the bowl must not leave the temple, and you will want to take it

temptations.cue: a tether from the steps
temptations.benefit: once, bind something so it cannot leave
temptations.standingDrawback: whatever you bind is now yours to give

temptations.cue: the ledger of what was given
temptations.benefit: once, prove a debt to the temple is paid
temptations.standingDrawback: an unpaid day of yours is written in it

temptations.cue: a stone from the bottom of the pit
temptations.benefit: once, survive something that should have taken you
temptations.standingDrawback: the pit is owed a substitution

silence.dangerLine: the name must not be said, and the temple is listening for it

institution: inscriptions with one word chiselled out of every line
a hall built to swallow sound rather than carry it
ritual: a rite performed entirely in gesture
a bell with the clapper removed and hung anyway
lips touched before crossing every threshold
demand: a room that makes your breathing audible
a veil you are expected to speak behind, not through
a doorway where your own voice does not follow you in
wound: jaws wired shut on every figure in a frieze
a mouth chiselled out of a statue and the hole smoothed
anchor: a veil that has never been lifted
a sealed box that hums when carried
a name written once and buried face-down

features: a hanging pulled aside and left
fresh wax on lips of a statue
a jar moved from a shelf
a clapper found on the floor
a word scratched into plaster and rubbed at
a door muffled with cloth, recently

decisions.cue: a veil you are expected to speak behind, not through
decisions.cost: speaking through it says the name into the room

resolve.success: you speak behind it correctly and the Tongueless treat you as initiated
resolve.failure: you speak through it and something hears its own name: roll the clock, +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: say nothing at all: safe, and you learn nothing

decisions.cue: an inscription with one word cut out of every line
decisions.cost: reconstructing the word is possible and is the whole point

resolve.success: you work it out and do not say it — knowing it is enough to open the way
resolve.failure: you say it aloud without meaning to: everything in the temple turns
resolve.orElse: leave it unreconstructed: one Turn to find another way

decisions.cue: a bell with the clapper hung beside it
decisions.cost: ringing it would be the loudest thing here in centuries

resolve.success: you strike it once, deliberately, and everything hostile withdraws for a scene
resolve.failure: the note goes on far too long and brings what it was meant to keep out
resolve.orElse: leave the clapper down; the silence holds

decisions.cue: a jar of tongues, counted, with a gap
decisions.cost: the count matters to something

resolve.success: you work out whose is missing and can use the name of the one who kept it
resolve.failure: you disturb the count and the Tongueless follow you thereafter
resolve.orElse: leave the jar; the count stays wrong

decisions.cue: a sealed box that hums when it is carried
decisions.cost: opening it is how the name got out last time

resolve.success: you carry it without opening it and it opens doors for you
resolve.failure: you open it: the name is loose in the room, +1 Bane and roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave it sealed and where it is

decisions.cue: a name written once and buried face-down
decisions.cost: turning it over reads it

resolve.success: you read it with your eyes only and hold something the temple fears
resolve.failure: you read it aloud out of habit: the temple stops treating you as a guest
resolve.orElse: leave it face-down; whatever is written stays buried

situations.doing: mouthing a word it cannot make a sound with
situations.onArrival: it takes your hand and shapes it into a gesture
situations.because: it kept the name and lost the means to say it
situations.offer: let it shape your hand and you will be able to say the word once, safely

situations.doing: doubling along the wall as you watch, muffling further
situations.onArrival: the room becomes noticeably quieter
situations.because: something is about to be said and must not be heard
situations.offer: speak first, quietly, and the hangings still

situations.doing: copying an inscription and leaving the cut-out word blank
situations.onArrival: they hold a finger to their lips and keep writing
situations.because: they know what the gap is and will not write it
situations.offer: promise not to say it and they will show you where it is written whole

situations.doing: standing empty behind a veil that moves without air
situations.onArrival: the veil bellies toward you
situations.because: something behind it is waiting to be addressed
situations.offer: address it without using any name and it will answer one question

situations.doing: standing in a line with their hands over their mouths
situations.onArrival: they part to let you through and do not lower their hands
situations.because: the silence must be kept by somebody
situations.offer: cover your own mouth and walk through, and they follow and guard you

situations.doing: hanging with its clapper on the floor beneath it
situations.onArrival: the bell moves very slightly
situations.because: the hour is due and cannot be struck
situations.offer: strike it with your hand — no clapper, no name — and the temple opens

temptations.cue: a length of the veil, unlifted
temptations.benefit: once, say something without anything hearing who said it
temptations.standingDrawback: your voice is not recognised by allies either

temptations.cue: a small sealed box that hums
temptations.benefit: once, open it and unmake something with a word
temptations.standingDrawback: the name is loose afterwards and looking for a mouth

temptations.cue: a bell clapper, heavy
temptations.benefit: once, make a sound that nothing here can ignore
temptations.standingDrawback: everything comes to see what rang

temptations.cue: a jar with one tongue in it
temptations.benefit: once, speak with the voice of whoever it belonged to
temptations.standingDrawback: they say something of their own each time

temptations.cue: a tablet, face-down, unread
temptations.benefit: once, read a name and know what it commands
temptations.standingDrawback: the name knows it has been read

exclusion.dangerLine: the temple will not share, and it can smell another god on you

institution: niches all along a wall, every one of them emptied
a floor of broken idols laid face-down as paving
a single lamp where a row of lamps was fixed
ritual: a censing of the doorway against something that keeps returning
tokens of other faiths collected in a basket at the door
a rite of exclusion cut beside every entrance
demand: a doorway that will not admit anything with two allegiances
a room where only one thing may be venerated at a time
a plinth built for one and made larger since
wound: idols broken carefully rather than in anger, and stacked
a frieze with every rival figure chiselled to a blank
a shrine walled up with the offerings still inside
anchor: a basket of confiscated tokens, still full
a list of gods forbidden here, complete

features: a niche recently emptied
a token dropped at the doorway
fresh mortar sealing a small shrine
broken idol-pieces sorted by size
a censer used at a door and left
a name scratched off a frieze, this year

decisions.cue: a basket at the door for tokens of other faiths
decisions.cost: giving up a token is a real cost to whoever carries it

resolve.success: you give one up properly and the temple treats the party as its own
resolve.failure: you keep one and it is smelled on you: the next encounter starts hostile
resolve.orElse: hand over everything: safe, and something you valued is gone

decisions.cue: a shrine walled up with the offerings still inside
decisions.cost: opening it frees a rival the temple beat

resolve.success: you open it and what is inside is grateful and useful
resolve.failure: you open it and the temple treats you as its enemy from here
resolve.orElse: leave it sealed; it has been sealed a long time

decisions.cue: a floor of broken idols laid face-down as paving
decisions.cost: turning one over is a small resurrection

resolve.success: you find one still whole beneath and it will speak for you once
resolve.failure: you turn over a broken one and it is angry with everybody
resolve.orElse: walk over them without looking; the temple approves

decisions.cue: the last idol standing, undamaged, and a hammer beside it
decisions.cost: the hammer was left there on purpose

resolve.success: you refuse the invitation and the temple is satisfied you are loyal
resolve.failure: you take up the hammer and something in the temple decides what you are
resolve.orElse: take the hammer away and hide it: the invitation stands for someone else

decisions.cue: a list of gods forbidden here, complete and long
decisions.cost: one of them is one you know

resolve.success: you find the name that matters and can use it against the temple later
resolve.failure: you are seen reading it and are assumed to be one of them: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: do not read the list; ignorance is safest here

decisions.cue: a censer at a doorway, still warm, used against something
decisions.cost: using it yourself declares a side

resolve.success: you cense the doorway and whatever keeps returning is held off for the delve
resolve.failure: you use it wrongly and it clears the way in instead
resolve.orElse: leave it; the door is uncensed and something uses it

situations.doing: emptying a niche that has been empty for centuries
situations.onArrival: it dusts the empty shelf and moves to the next
situations.because: the niches must be kept clear
situations.offer: help it dust and it will show you where what was in them went

situations.doing: standing assembled wrongly from pieces off the floor
situations.onArrival: the assembly shifts as you look at it
situations.because: it has been trying to stand up for a long time
situations.offer: assemble it correctly and it will owe you, and it is still strong

situations.doing: hiding a token in a wall before going in
situations.onArrival: they beg you, silently, not to say anything
situations.because: they cannot give it up and cannot carry it in
situations.offer: hide it better for them and they will guide you inside

situations.doing: standing alone on a plinth built for a row
situations.onArrival: the lamp before it is freshly lit
situations.because: it outlasted the others and knows it
situations.offer: praise it aloud and it will let you pass anywhere in the temple

situations.doing: filling further than when you last passed it
situations.onArrival: something in it is yours
situations.because: the confiscation continues without a doorkeeper
situations.offer: take back only what is yours and the temple allows it

situations.doing: chiselling a rival's name off a frieze it has already cleared
situations.onArrival: it hands you the chisel and points at a blank
situations.because: the frieze must be clean and always has more names
situations.offer: chisel one blank and it will name every god it drove out

temptations.cue: a small idol, undamaged
temptations.benefit: once, be protected as the temple protects its own
temptations.standingDrawback: you may carry no other token while you hold it

temptations.cue: a confiscated token from the basket
temptations.benefit: once, call on a god this temple hates
temptations.standingDrawback: the temple knows, and stops treating you as a guest

temptations.cue: the hammer left beside the idol
temptations.benefit: once, break something that should not be breakable
temptations.standingDrawback: the temple counts you a breaker of gods, approvingly

temptations.cue: the list of forbidden gods
temptations.benefit: once, name what something is afraid of
temptations.standingDrawback: you are assumed to worship whatever you name

temptations.cue: a face-down idol-fragment
temptations.benefit: once, hide your allegiance entirely
temptations.standingDrawback: nothing recognises you, including help
